column2: Light and shadow as the mechanism: a sculpture or object that casts the time as its shadow (think Mojoptix's digital sundial, or Kumi Yamashita's shadow art). The light source moves; the shadow is the reading.
Chinese calligraphy: a brush writes the time in Chinese characters on rice paper, wet ink bleeding into the fibres, the rhythm of real stroke order, seals in vermilion.
A newspaper crossword being solved in pencil and ink: the time is spelled in words in the grid, clues and crossings, erasures and corrections.
Music as the clock: a player-piano roll, a music box cylinder, or a score being played. The time is written in the music itself and performed.
Glitch art: datamoshing, pixel sorting, broken video compression, macroblocks, smeared motion vectors. The time survives, or is born from, the corruption.
An isometric pixel-art world (SimCity 2000, Habbo, Monument Valley): a tiny living city or place where the time is built, lit, zoned or traffic-jammed into being.
A 16-bit arcade fighting game (Street Fighter II era): two fighters, health bars, a round timer, special moves, KO screens. Hours versus minutes?
A vertical or horizontal bullet-hell shmup (Touhou, Ikaruga): dense, gorgeous danmaku patterns, a tiny ship weaving through them, a boss whose spell cards are the time.
A snow globe on a shelf: shaken, the flakes swirl and slowly settle, and where they settle is the time. Glass, water, light, physics.
Rorschach inkblot test cards: ink is dropped, the card folds and opens, a symmetric blot blooms. What do you see in it? The time.
A 1950s-60s film title sequence in the style of Saul Bass (Vertigo, Anatomy of a Murder, North by Northwest): cut-paper shapes, bold colour fields, jazzy rhythm, kinetic type.
Synthwave / outrun: neon wireframe grid racing to a striped sunset, chrome type, palm silhouettes, VHS glow, an 80s drive at night.
A kaleidoscope: tumbling coloured glass seen through mirrors, perfect symmetry that shifts as it turns. The time appears in the symmetry.
A pencil flipbook on a notebook corner, riffled by a thumb: rough hand-drawn animation, page curl, paper texture, the doodles evolving into the time.
A night skyscraper or apartment block seen across the street: hundreds of lit windows, lives inside them, lights switching on and off. The building is the display.
A Rube Goldberg machine: every minute a chain reaction of marbles, levers, dominoes, pulleys, candles and birds runs across the strip and changes the time.
